def-glm-observation-family:
## Definition

Fix a finite integer $n\ge1$ and a dispersion value $\phi$. For each $1\le i\le n$, let $\mathcal Y_i\subseteq\mathbb R$ carry its Borel sigma algebra and let $\nu_i$ be a sigma-finite positive measure on it. Let $J\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an open interval, let $b:J\to\mathbb R$ be twice continuously differentiable, let $a_i(\phi)>0$, and let $c_i(\,\cdot\,,\phi)$ be measurable. An **explicit one-parameter exponential-family response contract** supplies, for each $\theta_i\in J$, a density or mass function relative to $\nu_i$,

$$f_i(y_i;\theta_i,\phi)=\exp\!\left\{\frac{y_i\theta_i-b(\theta_i)}{a_i(\phi)}+c_i(y_i,\phi)\right\}.$$

The contract requires $f_i\ge0$, $\int f_i(\,\cdot\,;\theta_i,\phi)\,d\nu_i=1$ for every $\theta_i\in J$, and a fixed support $S_i\in\mathcal A_i$ such that $f_i>0$ on $S_i$ and $f_i=0$ off $S_i$, up to a $\nu_i$-null set independent of $\theta_i$. When the mean and variance identities are used, it also requires a finite second moment and locally uniform integrable envelopes for the first and second $\theta_i$ derivatives of $f_i$ on $S_i$.

For a vector $\theta=(\theta_1,\ldots,\theta_n)\in J^n$, the **product sampling law** is the finite product $\bigotimes_{i=1}^n P_{i,\theta_i,\phi}$, where $P_{i,\theta_i,\phi}$ has density $f_i$ relative to $\nu_i$. The coordinate responses are independent in the sense of [[def-independent-random-elements]]. Their product base measure is $\nu=\bigotimes_{i=1}^n\nu_i$ on $\bigotimes_{i=1}^n\mathcal A_i$. The next lemma verifies that the joint density is $\prod_i f_i$.

The design or conditioning convention, observation units, and response/index roles are part of the surrounding scientific model contract. A sampling-law specification is not evidence that the scientific model is empirically adequate.

Every scientific application also records a [[def-scientific-statistical-model-contract]]: it names the observation space and record, scientific and analysis units, index meanings, response and predictor maps, target, observation mechanism, support, law, conditioning, and adequacy assumptions. The contract does not itself imply independence or common support; those are explicit hypotheses of this response-family definition. Here $i$ is only a component index until the application assigns it a scientific unit or time meaning.
lem-glm-mean-and-variance-identities:
## Statement

Fix $i$ and $\phi$ in [[def-glm-observation-family]], and write $a=a_i(\phi)$. Under its fixed-support, twice differentiable density, local integrable derivative-envelope, and finite-second-moment hypotheses,

$$\mathbb E_{\theta_i,\phi}[Y_i]=b'(\theta_i),\qquad \operatorname{Var}_{\theta_i,\phi}(Y_i)=a\,b''(\theta_i).$$
lem-glm-product-density:
## Statement

In the setup of [[def-glm-observation-family]], let $P_\theta=\bigotimes_{i=1}^nP_{i,\theta_i,\phi}$ and $\nu=\bigotimes_{i=1}^n\nu_i$. Then the joint sampling law has density

$$q_\theta(y_1,\ldots,y_n)=\prod_{i=1}^n f_i(y_i;\theta_i,\phi)$$

relative to $\nu$. On the common product support $\prod_iS_i$, its log likelihood is $\sum_i\log f_i(y_i;\theta_i,\phi)$.
def-generalized-linear-model:
## Definition

Fix $n\ge1$, $p\ge1$, a finite design matrix $X\in\mathbb R^{n\times p}$ with rows $x_i^\mathsf T$, a dispersion value $\phi$, and an open parameter domain $\Theta\subseteq\mathbb R^p$. A **generalized linear model (GLM)** on this design consists of the response family in [[def-glm-observation-family]], a differentiable one-to-one link $g:\mathcal M\to g(\mathcal M)$ on a specified mean domain $\mathcal M$, and a specified map $\tau:\mathcal M\to J$ satisfying $b'(\tau(\mu))=\mu$. For $\beta\in\Theta$, put

$$\eta_i=x_i^\mathsf T\beta,\qquad \mu_i=g^{-1}(\eta_i),\qquad \theta_i=\tau(\mu_i),$$

and require $\eta_i\in g(\mathcal M)$ and $\theta_i\in J$ for every $i$. The **canonical link** is the choice $g=\tau$, equivalently $\theta_i=\eta_i$. When $\theta_i=\eta_i$ and the component scales are common, write $a_i(\phi)=a(\phi)>0$; this common-scale restriction is part of every formula that uses $a(\phi)$.

The joint sampling density is the product density from [[lem-glm-product-density]], and its log likelihood at an observed $y=(y_1,\ldots,y_n)$ in the common support is

$$\ell(\beta;y,\phi)=\sum_{i=1}^n\left\{\frac{y_i\theta_i-b(\theta_i)}{a_i(\phi)}+c_i(y_i,\phi)\right\}.$$

For a differentiable log likelihood, the **score** is $U(\beta;y,\phi):=\nabla_\beta\ell(\beta;y,\phi)$. When its entries have finite second moments, the **expected score outer-product information** is $I(\beta,\phi):=\mathbb E_{\beta,\phi}[U U^\mathsf T]$. This page treats $X$ as fixed or conditions on its realized value; it supplies no random-design asymptotic conclusion.
def-nested-model-deviance:
## Definition

Fix an observed response vector $y$ in a common support and two stated GLMs with the same response family, base support, and log-likelihood function $\ell(\beta;y)$. They are **nested** here only when a stated embedding identifies the fitted parameter set with a subset $\Theta_{\mathrm{fit}}\subseteq\Theta_{\mathrm{sat}}$ of the saturated reference parameter set. Require both sets to be nonempty and both suprema to be finite real numbers. The **likelihood deviance** is

$$D(y)=2\left\{\sup_{\beta\in\Theta_{\mathrm{sat}}}\ell(\beta;y)-\sup_{\beta\in\Theta_{\mathrm{fit}}}\ell(\beta;y)\right\}.$$

The definition makes no claim about deviance residuals, goodness-of-fit diagnostics, or a reference distribution. The two full-text GLM notes cited above support likelihood setup but do not supply a deviance-diagnostics treatment; the nonnegativity result below is proved only from the stated set inclusion.
thm-canonical-glm-score-and-hessian:
## Statement

Let $(Y_i)_{i=1}^n$ follow [[def-generalized-linear-model]] with a common scale $a(\phi)>0$, canonical link $\theta_i=\eta_i=x_i^\mathsf T\beta$, and twice differentiable $b$. Then, for $y$ in the common support,

$$\nabla_\beta\ell(\beta;y,\phi)=\frac{X^\mathsf T(y-\mu)}{a(\phi)},\qquad \nabla_\beta^2\ell(\beta;y,\phi)=-\frac{X^\mathsf T\operatorname{diag}(b''(\eta_i))X}{a(\phi)}.$$
thm-glm-general-link-score-and-informati:
## Statement

Consider [[def-generalized-linear-model]] at an admissible finite $\beta$ with common scale $a(\phi)>0$. Assume each $\eta_i\mapsto\theta_i$ is differentiable, each $\eta_i\mapsto\mu_i$ is differentiable with $\dot\mu_i:=d\mu_i/d\eta_i\ne0$, $V_i:=b''(\theta_i)>0$, the component scores have finite second moments, and the common-support, differentiability, and local integrable derivative-envelope conditions from [[def-glm-observation-family]] hold. Put

$$w_i=\frac{\dot\mu_i^2}{a(\phi)V_i},\qquad z_i=\eta_i+\frac{y_i-\mu_i}{\dot\mu_i}.$$

Then the score and expected score outer-product information are

$$U(\beta;y,\phi)=X^\mathsf T\left(\frac{\dot\mu_i(y_i-\mu_i)}{a(\phi)V_i}\right)_{i=1}^n,\qquad I(\beta,\phi)=X^\mathsf T\operatorname{diag}(w_i)X.$$

In particular, if $X$ has full column rank, then $I$ is positive definite.
alg-fisher-scoring-irls:
## Definition

Inputs are an observed response vector $y$ in the common support, a finite design matrix $X$, an admissible finite current parameter $\beta$, and a GLM with common scale $a(\phi)>0$. Require each $\dot\mu_i=d\mu_i/d\eta_i$ to be finite and nonzero and each $V_i=b''(\theta_i)$ to be finite and positive.

1. Compute $\eta_i=x_i^\mathsf T\beta$ and $\mu_i=g^{-1}(\eta_i)$.
2. Compute the **working response** and positive weight
$$z_i=\eta_i+\frac{y_i-\mu_i}{\dot\mu_i},\qquad w_i=\frac{\dot\mu_i^2}{a(\phi)V_i}.$$
3. Form $W^{1/2}=\operatorname{diag}(\sqrt{w_i})$ using [[thm-of-square-roots]], and put $A=W^{1/2}X$, $r=W^{1/2}z$. By [[def-moore-penrose-pseudoinverse]] and [[thm-moore-penrose-pseudoinverse-exists-and-is-unique]], form $A^+$. Return $\beta_{\mathrm{new}}=A^+r$, the unique minimum-Euclidean-norm member of the nonempty weighted least-squares minimizer set by [[thm-a-plus-b-is-the-unique-minimum-norm-least-squares-solution]].

The Moore--Penrose convention makes the procedure single-valued even when $X$ is rank deficient; the underlying least-squares minimizer need not then be unique. Existence and the minimum-norm property follow from [[thm-moore-penrose-pseudoinverse-exists-and-is-unique]] and [[thm-a-plus-b-is-the-unique-minimum-norm-least-squares-solution]]. When the information is invertible, this output is the ordinary unique Fisher-scoring step. The output need not lie in $\Theta$, and this definition makes no claim that repeated updates terminate or converge to a maximizer.
thm-canonical-glm-strict-concavity:
## Statement

Suppose the canonical-link GLM has an open convex parameter domain $\Theta\subseteq\mathbb R^p$, full-column-rank design $X$, common scale $a(\phi)>0$, and $b''(\eta_i)>0$ at every predictor vector in $X\Theta$. Then $\ell(\,\cdot\,;y,\phi)$ is strictly concave on $\Theta$. It has at most one stationary point; if a stationary point exists, it is the unique global maximizer. This conclusion does not assert that a finite maximizer exists.
thm-irls-is-fisher-scoring-step:
## Statement

Under the admissibility hypotheses of [[alg-fisher-scoring-irls]], if $I(\beta)=X^\mathsf T W X$ is invertible, let $U(\beta)$ and $I(\beta)$ be the score and expected score outer-product information from [[thm-glm-general-link-score-and-information]]. Then the weighted least-squares output satisfies

$$\beta_{\mathrm{new}}=\beta+I(\beta)^{-1}U(\beta).$$
